I read the whole file and checked it against the rubric. I did not search the Mathlib sources, so this rests on the file's own text and my knowledge of Mathlib.

- The only new data type is the private structure `struct`. It packages a sequence of objects `X n`, elements `x n`, effective epimorphisms `map n : X (n+1) ⟶ X n`, and compatibility conditions `w n`. It is internal scaffolding for one proof. It is not a general concept, and I know of no Mathlib structure with the same shape.
- `preimage`, `preimageStruct`, `preimageDiagram` and `cone` are private constructions for this one argument. They build on existing Mathlib pieces: `Functor.ofOpSequence`, `NatTrans.ofOpSequence`, `GrothendieckTopology.yonedaEquiv` and `Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective`. They do not duplicate those pieces.
- The two public lemmas are theorems, not competing definitions. Duplicating a theorem is outside this rubric.
- I found no competing version of an existing concept, so I report nothing.
